used_for: Why a gap is not a complete answer

evidence.excerpt: Consider a sentence named ‘FLiar’, which says of itself (i.e., says of FLiar) that it is false.
An obvious response is to deny that every sentence is true or false, i.e., to deny the principle of bivalence.

Rather than work with falsehood, we can construct a Liar sentence with the complex predicate ‘not true’.[2] Consider a sentence named ‘ULiar’ (for ‘un-true’), which says of itself that it is not true.
Even so, every sentence is either true or something other than true, i.e. not true.
But this is what ULiar says, so we conclude ULiar, from which we infer that ULiar is true, which is a contradiction.
